content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Status: deviation (high severity) — Section 2 grant, read with Sections 3(c) and 20(d)**

What the licence already gets right:
- **Affiliates are expressly covered** — "for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations." This actually beats the fallback, which would only require affiliates on written notice.
- **Not revocable at will** — Section 17(a) makes the licence perpetual so long as fees are paid, and termination is confined to insolvency events or a material default uncured after thirty days' notice. p0128 goes further in our favour: if we terminate for Garman's default, the licence converts to a fee-free perpetual licence and prepaid fees for unrendered services are returned.

Why it still fails the fallback:
- **No successor transferability.** The grant is expressly "non-transferable," Section 3(c) bars assignment, transfer or sublicence without Garman's written consent, and Section 20(d) has no M&A carve-out. The fallback requires transferability to a successor in an M&A transaction, so licence continuity through a merger or sale of the business currently sits entirely at Garman's discretion. This is the material failure.
- **Contractors unnamed.** A preferred-position shortfall rather than walk-away, since Section 3(c) leaves a consent path — but worth fixing in the same pass.

The validated redline makes three small edits: contractors added to the grant, "non-transferable" replaced with a successor-transfer right, a matching carve-out in Section 20(d), plus a conforming cross-reference in Section 3(c) so the restriction does not contradict the new grant language. The Authorized Locations structure and additional-fee mechanic for other locations are untouched, as is the general consent requirement for ordinary assignments.

One drafting note for the negotiation: the grant ties affiliate and contractor use to "operating at Authorized Locations," and use elsewhere triggers additional fees under the Fee Schedule. If contractors are expected to support the AS400s remotely rather than from a listed site, that location gating may need separate attention.
